advisory.finding: The operator /rerun (and contributor recheck-review) can now be refused with HTTP 409 'nonzero vote remains' whenever ANY account retains a nonzero LLM-Review vote, because reset_llm_review_vote only zeroes the bot's own vote while has_llm_review_vote inspects all accounts. This contradicts the documented 'unrestricted semantics' of the /rerun escape hatch and makes the recovery path blockable by a human/admin vote it cannot clear.

reconcile.py:263-264 `if await asyncio.to_thread(gc.has_llm_review_vote, change_id, revision):` — now executed for every candidate in the loop `for change_id, ev in candidates.items():` (reconcile.py:253).

The module docstring change (reconcile.py:44-50) confirms: 'For each bounded events-log candidate it queries Gerrit FIRST.' — Gerrit is contacted per candidate, whereas the prior local dedup pre-filter avoided the round-trip for already-recorded changes.

advisory.finding: The reconciler removed the cheap local already_voted pre-filter and now issues a Gerrit has_llm_review_vote REST call for EVERY candidate on every poll, instead of only for candidates lacking a local dedup row.
merged_from: The reconciler removed the cheap local `already_voted` SQLite pre-filter, so every candidate in the events-log window now incurs a synchronous Gerrit `has_llm_review_vote` HTTP round-trip each poll (one remote call per candidate), instead of short-circuiting the already-voted majority locally. app.py distinguishes the codes: `return JSONResponse(status_code=502, content={"status": "vote reset failed"})` (src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:369), `status_code=502` for verification (app.py:380), and `return JSONResponse(status_code=409, content={"status": "nonzero vote remains"})` (app.py:387)
Regression-blindness: the reconcile/retrigger paths distinguish these fault classes, but the app-path test collapses them to a single non-202 assertion
advisory.finding: The parametrized /rerun refuse test asserts only `resp.status_code != 202`, so it cannot detect a regression in the distinct HTTP status contract the code implements: 502 for a reset/verification GerritError vs 409 for a surviving nonzero vote. A change that returned 409 for a reset failure (or 502 for a nonzero-vote) would still pass.
scenarios: A refactor mislabels a nonzero-vote refusal as 502 (or a transient Gerrit fault as a client-side 409) and clients/operators misinterpret retryability
advisory.suggested_fix: Parametrize an expected status alongside `failure` (e.g. `("reset", 502), ("read", 502), ("nonzero", 409)`) and assert `resp.status_code == expected`, mirroring how the retrigger test asserts the specific `reason`.
